title: Delete with one delegated listener
prompt:
Each expense has a Delete button. The starter attaches a listener to each button, but `renderExpenses` replaces the buttons after the first delete, so the second delete does nothing, and new expenses can never be deleted.

Replace the loop at the bottom with **one** click listener on `#expense-list`. When a click lands on (or inside) a `.delete` button, remove that expense from `expenses` using the item's `data-id`, then call `renderExpenses()`. Clicks elsewhere in the list must do nothing.
hints: Attach it to the list, which is never replaced: `list.addEventListener("click", (event) => { … });`.
`event.target.closest(".delete")` gives the button, or `null` if the click was not on one. Return early when it is `null`.
The id is on the `<li>`: `button.closest("li").dataset.id`. Then `expenses = expenses.filter((e) => e.id !== id);` and `renderExpenses();`.
explanation: The list element is created once by the HTML and never replaced, so a listener on it survives every render. Clicks on any Delete button bubble up to it, including buttons for expenses that did not exist when the listener was added. `closest(".delete")` finds the button even if the click landed on something inside it, and returns `null` for clicks on the label, which the early `return` ignores. The handler changes only the data and then re-renders, so the list and the total always agree with `expenses`.

checks.first-delete: Deleting an expense removes it and updates the total
checks.second-delete: A second delete still works after the list re-rendered
checks.new-items: Expenses added later can be deleted too
checks.ignore-other-clicks: Clicking an item's label deletes nothing
checks.data-updated: The expenses array itself is updated, not just the page
